messages:
Vanessa Ortiz: hey all — looping back on burst pools. we need to sanity check procurement constraints + how big the safety buffers should be per region given supply risk. current sizing doc is using a flat 15% buffer across regions/hw and i don’t think that’s realistic.

Jamal Pierce: +1. “buffer” is doing two jobs right now: (1) supply/procurement variability (can we actually backfill pool when utilization rises) and (2) operational headroom (failures / maintenance / telemetry lag). those should probably be separate knobs.

Harish Reddy: from ops side: US regions are still easiest to top up, EU is slower, APAC is basically “don’t count on it.” even within US, us-east is meaningfully better than us-west on H100 availability.

Keiko Yamamoto: for guardrails, we can keep the fleet safety cap conservative, but if pools are sized too tight in high-risk regions we’ll create constant denials + oncall noise. would rather be explicit: higher buffer in risky regions, lower in stable.

Vanessa Ortiz: agreed. can we align on a default “supply risk multiplier” by region + hardware class? thinking something like:
- us-east H100: low risk
- us-west H100: medium
- eu-west H100/L40S: high
- ap-southeast anything: very high

Rishi Malhotra: finance POV: higher buffers = idle cost. we’re ok with it if we can tie it to quantified risk + customer promise (SLA language). but we should avoid “blanket +30% everywhere.”

Lauren Bishop: product question: does this change what we tell customers? e.g. “burst available” but denial rates are higher in EU? we probably need a consistent story + region-specific expectations in the console.

Harish Reddy: procurement constraints summary (as of this month):
- H100 us-east: we can usually add small increments in 2–4 weeks (not guaranteed, but decent)
- H100 us-west: 4–8 weeks, sometimes longer
- L40S eu-west: 6–10 weeks and supply is lumpy
- H100 eu-west: basically 8–12+ weeks; allocations get reshuffled
so if pool is trending hot, EU can’t recover quickly.

Jamal Pierce: propose we model buffer as:
`buffer_total = buffer_ops + buffer_supply`
where:
- buffer_ops is fixed per pool (e.g. 10% for maintenance/failover/noise)
- buffer_supply varies (e.g. 5% low / 15% med / 25% high / 35% very high)
then utilization target is separate (e.g. aim 60–70% average pool utilization).

Keiko Yamamoto: if we do that, we should also tighten admission when telemetry is stale. supply risk buffer shouldn’t be used to mask control-plane lag / bad signals. (we got burned by that in beta.)

Vanessa Ortiz: yup. also important: procurement “buffer” isn’t just lead time — it’s also cancellation risk + vendor “oops we moved your allocation.” EU is worst there.

CapPlanBot: FYI: Fleet forecast run (2025-02-18) shows eu-west H100 utilization trending +9% WoW due to 2 Dedicated renewals. Risk flag: HIGH. Recommended action: increase safety buffer or reduce burst cap.

Rishi Malhotra: if we take the “very high” buffer to 35% in APAC, we should confirm we’re not overbuilding a region that’s low revenue today. can we instead cap burst ratios more aggressively there?

Keiko Yamamoto: we can do both. for very high supply risk regions: lower max burst ratio (e.g. 1.25x baseline) + higher buffer (so that allowed burst actually works when enabled). otherwise we’re selling a feature that just 429s.

Lauren Bishop: +1. “burst that doesn’t burst” is worse than “burst not available in that region.” we can put region/hw availability in the packaging sheet + console.

Harish Reddy: operationally, i’d prefer: in high-risk regions we keep pool small + buffer higher, AND we keep a hard circuit breaker earlier. also helps protect neighbor workloads.

Jamal Pierce: numbers strawman (open to debate):
- buffer_ops: 10% across the board
- buffer_supply (by region risk tier): low 5%, med 10%, high 20%, very high 30%
=> total buffer: 15/20/30/40%
that’s more than today, but we stop pretending EU == us-east.

Vanessa Ortiz: feels directionally right. i’d tweak high to 25% and very high to 35% given what Harish said about EU/APAC “recovery time.” total buffers 35/45% in those tiers.

Rishi Malhotra: 45% buffer is going to get questions. if we do that, i want it explicitly linked to: (a) contractual non-burst SLO protection and (b) expected denial rate targets. e.g. “we keep X% buffer to ensure denials < Y% at planned peak.”

Keiko Yamamoto: from guardrails side we can set an SLO target for burst pools: “admission success rate >= 95% for tenants within their configured caps when pool saturation < 80% and telemetry is healthy.” then buffer is what keeps saturation from living at 95%.

Harish Reddy: also keep in mind maintenance windows: EU has more forced maintenance churn (datacenter constraints). ops buffer probably can’t be flat 10% if we’re honest.

Jamal Pierce: ok so we may end up with:
- buffer_ops: 10% low/med, 15% high/very-high
- buffer_supply: 5/10/25/35
=> totals: 15%, 20%, 40%, 50% (worst case)
we should run that through the sizing model and see idle cost.

Vanessa Ortiz: action items:
1) Jamal: update sizing model v1 to separate ops vs supply buffers + add region risk tier input.
2) Harish: drop a short note on current lead times by region/hw (can go into the policy doc).
3) Keiko: propose default max burst ratios per tier (low/med/high/vhigh) so we can trade buffer vs caps.
4) Rishi: sanity check margin impact with the new buffer tiers.

Lauren Bishop: and i’ll sync w/ Console team on how we expose “availability/expected behavior by region” without scaring customers. :thumbsup:

Rishi Malhotra: works. pls include a table we can point to in approvals (something like: risk tier -> buffer -> cap -> rationale).

Keiko Yamamoto: will do. also note: these should be overrideable by fleet safety kill switch per region if procurement surprises us.

Harish Reddy: yep. procurement surprises are the default :)

Vanessa Ortiz: lol. ok thanks all — let’s aim to have the updated table by end of week so it can go into the burst pool sizing policy + PRD appendix.
